source.title: Quantifying and Optimizing Simplicity via Polynomial Representations
source.authors: Tian-Ren Zhang; Xiangxing Li; Ming-Hao Xiao; Guanyu Chen; Feng Chen

record.tranche_reason: Measures correlations between post-hoc complexity measures and generalization gap using a different model pool and training setup from the version’s stated study.
record.gate_note: The study’s own correlation analysis bears on V7. Its ED-regularization results are not rows for the listed versions: those versions do not cover polynomial-complexity regularization. The paper also discusses other work on memorization, optimizers, batch size and regularization; those cited findings are not this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The ResNet18 analysis tests V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–gap relationship using adaptive sharpness at fixed perturbation radii rather than perturbation tolerance at a fixed error increase. Transformer results extend beyond V7's stated convolutional-network scope.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the correlation findings. The authors additionally conclude that effective degree provides a differentiable regularizer that improves performance across their tested vision, text, and reinforcement-learning tasks. Their MNIST–CIFAR experiment identifies a failure case: regularization does not overcome reliance on a simpler, less robust feature.
record.recipe_differences: Post-hoc Pearson correlation analysis across hyperparameter configurations and fine-tuning recipes, rather than magnitude-scaled weight perturbation tolerance among same-family networks with similarly low training loss.
record.method_sensitivity: Model and training recipe change the correlations: CLIP sharpness measures correlate negatively with the gap, whereas CIFAR-10 ResNet18 and ViT-Tiny show positive correlations.

fits_no_version.finding: Standard sharpness correlates positively with the ResNet18 generalization gap (r = 0.94).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unscaled fixed-radius sharpness predicts generalization gaps in this ResNet18 model pool.

fits_no_version.finding: Adaptive sharpness correlates positively with the gap for ViT-Tiny (0.83), but negatively for fine-tuned CLIP with mixup (approximately -0.50) and without mixup (approximately -0.38).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The direction of the adaptive-sharpness relationship varies across transformer training and fine-tuning settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Standard sharpness and parameter norms also show architecture-dependent correlations in transformer settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter-space generalization proxies vary in reliability across transformer model pools.

fits_no_version.finding: Effective degree has positive correlations of 0.99, 0.85, 0.93, and 0.71 across the four reported model pools.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Polynomial effective degree predicts generalization gaps across the tested image-classification settings.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The study’s correlation analysis uses proxy measures across varied configurations rather than the specific perturbation-tolerance measure in V7. Numerical confidence interval bounds are not given in the supplied text; they are shown in figures. The study does not establish causality.

untested.parts: Matched random-label fitting, natural-label generalization, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the interpolation threshold.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Controlled optimizer comparisons under limited or broader tuning.
Held-out performance by batch size under matched epoch budgets and adapted recipes; batch sizes enter the correlation pool but no corresponding performance comparison is reported.

The original perturbation-tolerance measure, margin-based comparisons, SVHN, and a pool explicitly restricted to similarly low training loss without augmentation. Pearson correlation does not directly reproduce the original ranking analysis.
Removing examples selected by memorization scores and comparing retrained accuracy with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: The figure confidence bands concern least-squares fitted lines, not explicitly confidence intervals on Pearson correlations. Correlations are selected over perturbation-radius sweeps; ED additionally benefits from variant selection. ED outperforming sharpness does not itself limit V7, which compares sharpness with norm- and margin-based measures. Transformer reversals do not challenge the explicitly scoped convolutional claim.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance.
Large versus small batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.

The study does not use the version’s specific perturbation-tolerance measure or compare only networks from one convolutional family with similarly low training loss. Its models and recipes include ViT and fine-tuned CLIP settings.

rows.measure: Correlation of standard sharpness with generalization gap
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals shown in Figure 2; numerical bounds not stated.
rows.note: The text states that ED showed the strongest correlation and outperformed both sharpness variants; exact correlation is labeled in the figure.
rows.check: Standard sharpness does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness. The CIFAR-10 correlation protocol does not establish the recorded mixup condition.

rows.measure: Correlation of adaptive sharpness with generalization gap
